title: Scheduled Tasks
description: Run a tool's work on a schedule, reliably, without a server you have to babysit — what cron actually promises, how serverless scheduled functions differ from a machine you own, and the three ways a scheduled job quietly stops being trustworthy: it overlaps itself, it stops firing and nobody notices, or it fires at the wrong hour because a time zone assumption was wrong.

title: Webhooks
description: Receive and verify webhooks from another service safely — what a webhook actually is from the receiving side, how to check a request really came from who it claims, why the endpoint has to answer fast and do the real work after, and how to handle the same event arriving more than once.

title: Sending Results to Slack
description: Deliver a tool's output into Slack in a form people actually read — the real difference between an incoming webhook and a full Slack app, formatting that survives being skimmed on a phone, respecting rate limits by batching instead of spamming a channel, handling a failed send without losing the result, and letting people configure where their own results go.

title: Sending Results by Email
description: Send transactional email people trust and don't mark as spam — how transactional email differs from marketing email under the rules that govern it, the deliverability basics that decide whether a message lands in the inbox at all, a template that survives a dozen different email clients, the law behind unsubscribe links, and what to do when an address stops working.

title: Chaining Automations
description: Connect several automated steps into one pipeline that fails safely — designing the chain, logging it so you can reconstruct what happened, retrying one step without redoing the rest, and deciding whether you'd actually trust it to run while you're asleep.
